en: Thus have I heard: At one time, the Bhagavān was staying on the bank of a river near Uruvilvā-maṅgala. The *Buddhabhāṣita-brāhmaṇa-jalaviśuddhi-parikalpa-sūtra*, translated by an unknown person and appended to the catalogue of the Eastern Jin, was heard as follows:
At one time, the Bhagavān was staying on the bank of a river near Uruvilvā-maṅgala.

While he was alone beneath a tree, having just attained perfect enlightenment, at that time there was a Brahmin named Jāṇussoṇī who, after his midday meal, was wandering along when he came to where the Blessed One was. The Blessed One saw from afar the Brahmin Jāṇussoṇī approaching.
Having seen the brahmin Jāṇussoṇī, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus for his sake:
"If one possesses twenty-one fetters that bind the mind, one shall fall into the evil destinies and be born in the hells."
What are the twenty-one? They are: the fetter of attachment to wrong views;

the desire for what is not the Dharma to deceive the world through false teachings; greed; ill-will; sloth; torpor; restlessness; lack of shame; doubt; resentment and anger; stinginess, envy, and refusal to relinquish; flattery and deceit; lack of modesty and lack of shame; excessive jealousy and envy; and the fetter of heedlessness.

If one possesses these twenty-one fetters and attachments of the mind, one will fall into the evil destinies and be born in hell, like a filthy garment worn by a small child. Suppose its owner gives it to a dyer or a dyer’s apprentice, who takes the garment and soaks it with salt-earth, cow dung, or clay, washing and rinsing it until it is utterly pure.

Even though that dyer and his apprentice take those soiled garments of the infant and wash them thoroughly until they are extremely clean using salt earth, ash, cow dung, and clay, those garments of the infant still retain their black grease.
In this way, if one possesses twenty-one fetters that bind the mind, one will fall into the evil destinies and be born in hell.
What are these twenty-one?
They range from the fetter of the mind being bound by wrong view to the fetter of the mind being bound by heedlessness.
If one possesses these twenty-one fetters and attachments of the mind, one will fall into the evil destinies and be born in the hells;
if one is without these twenty-one fetters and attachments of the mind, one will instead be born in a good place, in the heavens.
What are the twenty-one?
They range from the fetter of attachment to the mind through wrong view to the fetter of attachment to the mind through negligence.
If one does not possess these twenty-one fetters that attach to the mind, one will be reborn in a favorable place, in the heavens.

It is just as when a garment is finished in Vārāṇasī, and its owner gives it to a dyer or a dyer’s apprentice; that dyer or apprentice takes it and soaks it with salt-earth, ash, and cow dung, then washes and rinses it until it is thoroughly clean.

Although that cloth was made in Vārāṇasī, when the dyer and his apprentice dye it, soaking it in salt water, ash, and cow dung, and washing and rinsing it thoroughly until it is clean, that cloth made in Vārāṇasī becomes extremely pure and white.
In this way, if there are those who are free from the twenty-one fetters and attachments of the mind, they will be reborn in a good destination, in the heavens.
What are these twenty-one?
From the mental fetter of wrong view up to the mental attachment of negligence—if one is free from these, one will be reborn in a good destination, in the heavens.

Having seen the fetter of the mind of wrong view, one should abandon it; having seen the fetter of attachment to the mind of negligence, one should abandon it. Then, that mind, accompanied by loving-kindness, dwells in right meditative attainment, suffusing one direction.

In this way, in the second, third, and fourth directions, above and below, and in all directions, his mind is accompanied by loving-kindness—without duality and without ill will—vast, expansive, immeasurable, and free from discrimination; having filled all directions, he dwells in right attainment.

In this way, having fully pervaded all directions with the mind accompanied by compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity, one dwells in right attainment; this is the purification of a brāhmaṇa both internally and externally, and not merely external purification.
“Śramaṇa Gautama! You have gone to the water to bathe.
“O brāhmaṇa! [he replied.]
"Gautama, those who wash with water do so because the entire world ought to observe precepts, ought to cultivate merit, and ought to attain liberation. "O Gautama!

As for those in the entire world who wash with water, they remove all evil; thus, immersing themselves in water to cleanse and moisten themselves is what the foolish and ignorant constantly delight in."
"This cannot eliminate black-and-black deeds; though one uses that water for purification, while it remains in the water, what does it see?
When a person commits various evil deeds, what power can this water have to purify them?"

Those who possess firm purity should maintain the practice of precepts and engage in pure conduct; by engaging in pure conduct, they will always remain in accordance with the precepts. If one refrains from killing, stealing, and false speech, one attains equal transcendence. O Brahmin, you should abide in this and perform all that is wholesome, so as to attain peace and security.
O Brahmin! Why must you return home?
What need have you for water or home?
O Brahmin! Why seek foul and evil water when you can seek pure and wholesome dharmas?
Simply remove the dust, defilement, and impurity.
"Gautama, you may think:
'It is better to seek pure and wholesome dharmas than to need foul and evil water to remove dust, grime, and filth.
This being so, Gautama!"
"I have finished, Gautama!
I now take refuge in the World-Honored One, the Dharma, and the Sangha of Bhikṣus.
World-Honored One!"
"I am a lay follower; from this day forth, for as long as life lasts, I shall abstain from taking life and take refuge in the Buddha.
Thus spoke the Buddha.
Having heard what the World-Honored One had said, those bhikṣus rejoiced and departed.
The Sūtra on the Brahmin’s Calculation of Water Purity Spoken by the Buddha.
